nodes.description: Lysosomal glycosphingolipid storage in saposin A-deficient cells causes at least a twofold expansion of LAMP1-positive lysosomal vesicles and blocks autophagic flux by impairing autophagosome-lysosome fusion (50-60% reduction in LAMP1/LC3A colocalization), leading to intracellular accumulation of LC3A- and p62-positive autophagosomes.

evidence.snippet: Autophagosome-lysosome fusion is impaired in saposin A-deficient fibroblasts. We demonstrated that the extent of LAMP1/LC3A colocalization was reduced (ranging from 50 to 60%) in the proband fibroblast compared to those of the father and brother (Fig. 6a, b).

evidence.snippet: Our data suggest that accumulation of autophagosomes (Fig. 5b, c) in saposin A-deficient fibroblasts is due to defective clearance caused by impaired autophagosome-lysosome fusion (Fig. 6a, b).

nodes.description: Saposin A is generated by proteolytic processing of prosaposin (encoded by PSAP) into four mature lysosomal activator glycoproteins (saposins A-D). Biallelic pathogenic variants in the saposin A-coding domain of PSAP abolish saposin A function, eliminating the essential in vivo cofactor required for galactosylceramidase (GALC) stabilization and substrate presentation despite a genetically intact GALC enzyme.
